content.text: {"primary_meaning":"Sacredness: belonging to or being set apart for God and therefore distinct from the ordinary or profane. In Christian teaching this commonly includes moral purity; when applied to God, it denotes his perfect purity, unique majesty, and transcendence.","primary_basis":["Leviticus 11:44-45; 19:2 — Israel is commanded to be holy because God is holy.","Exodus 3:5 — ground is holy because of God’s presence.","Exodus 19:5-6 — Israel is designated a holy nation belonging especially to God.","Isaiah 6:1-7 — the threefold proclamation of God’s holiness is associated with his majesty and the cleansing of impurity.","1 Peter 1:15-16; 2:9 — Christians are called to holy conduct and described as a holy nation.","Hebrews 12:14 — holiness is presented as necessary for seeing the Lord.","Revelation 4:8 — heavenly worship proclaims God as holy three times."] ,"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Moral purity or sinlessness, treated as the principal meaning rather than as a consequence of consecration to God.","basis":["Leviticus 19:2-18 links holiness with ethical commandments.","1 Peter 1:14-16 connects holiness with obedient conduct.","Hebrews 12:14 and Ephesians 1:4 associate holiness with blameless life."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"God’s absolute otherness, transcendence, and incomparable majesty.","basis":["Isaiah 6:1-5 presents holiness amid divine enthronement, awe, and human unworthiness.","Isaiah 40:25 associates the Holy One with divine incomparability.","Revelation 4:8-11 joins holiness with sovereignty, eternity, and worship."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Consecration for a specific divine purpose or service, without necessarily implying intrinsic moral perfection.","basis":["Exodus 29:37; 30:29-30 describes altars, objects, and priests as holy through consecration.","Numbers 6:5-8 describes the Nazirite as holy through dedication.","1 Corinthians 7:14 uses “holy” of family members in a covenantal or relational sense."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The manifestation or sphere of God’s special presence, so that places, times, objects, or people are called holy because God is present or claims them.","basis":["Exodus 3:5 identifies ground as holy at the divine appearance.","Exodus 25:8; 26:33-34 concerns the sanctuary and Most Holy Place.","Psalm 99:5,9 associates holiness with God’s throne and holy mountain."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Wholeness, completeness, or integrated spiritual health as the root symbolic meaning of holiness.","basis":["This is sometimes proposed in devotional or theological treatments, but it is not the standard lexical explanation of the biblical Hebrew and Greek terms."],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is a settled broad consensus, though not a single exhaustive definition. The meanings “set apart for or belonging to God,” “sacred,” “morally pure,” and “divinely transcendent” overlap and vary with context. “Holy” is ordinarily treated as a theological and relational descriptor rather than as a symbol with one fixed allegorical referent."}
